en: The Goddess said: O God, how is the unsurpassed [state] that immediately bestows the Kaulika perfection, by the mere realization of which one attains equality with the Sky-farer (Khecarī)? ParTri_1 //
O Lord, tell me this secret, the great secret:
that power which resides in the heart, Kaulinī, the mistress of the Kula. (Parātrīśikā 2)
"Tell that to me, O Lord of Gods, so that I may attain satisfaction.
Śrī Bhairava said:
"Listen, O Goddess of great fortune, to the unsurpassed [teaching] even beyond the North. (ParTri 3)
This Kaulika rite, which abides within the sky of my heart, I shall declare without doubt; it bestows the immediate attainment of the Kaula. (Parātrīśikā 4)
Now, all the initial lunar days (tithis) consist of the vowels ending with the bindu;
within them, through the conjunction of time, the Moon and Sun are proclaimed. (Parātriṃśikā 5)
O lady of excellent vows, the principles beginning with earth and ending with the Puruṣa reside respectively in the consonant groups beginning with *ka* and ending with *ma*.
There is a quartet of meditative concentrations (dhāraṇās) on air, fire, water, and Indra;
above that is the well-known [series] beginning with *śa*, and in front is the pentad of Brahmā.
[Var.
7cd: upward] That sequence should be known as rootless; it is declared to be the emanation (*sṛṣṭi*) of *kṣāntā*, O illustrious lady, for all mantras and vidyās alike. (ParTri 8)
This source has been fully proclaimed in all tantras at all times,
O auspicious one, as being joined with the fourteen and endowed with the end of the lords of the lunar days.
O fair-hipped one, this third [revelation] is the heart of the Bhairava-self, the Brahman; clearly, neither one born of a Yoginī nor one who is not Rudra attains this. (Parātrīṃśikā 10)
The heart-mantra of the God of gods bestows immediate liberation through yoga;
when it is properly uttered, the great multitude of mantras and mudrās [is activated]. (ParTri 11)
He who is sealed by the Kisser (Cumbaka) remembers for a moment that which leads to the characteristic of entering one's own body, and immediately attains the state of being its very mouth.
Then that person binds the body with the multitude of mantras and mudrās;
when questioned, he even speaks of matters past and future.
By reciting the intended form of the deity for one watch [of the night],
one sees it directly and without doubt, drawn forth by the powers of Rudra.
By recollecting [this] for merely two watches (six hours), one becomes established in the sky;
by three watches, all the Mothers, the powerful mistresses of yoga, [appear].
The heroes, the lords of heroes, the perfected ones, and the powerful host of Śākinīs,
having been impelled by Bhairava, arrived and gave their pledge.
They bestow supreme accomplishment or whatever fruit is desired; by means of this, accomplished practitioners have attained success, will attain it, and are now attaining it. (ParTri 17)
Whatever exists in the Bhairava Tantra, all of that is accomplished through this.
Even one who has not seen the maṇḍala, whoever knows this according to reality, shall eternally possess accomplishment; he is a yogi and he is initiated. (Parātriṃśikā 18)
By the mere knowledge of this, one is known by all the powers;
indeed, one becomes a member of the common assembly of the Śākinīs even without [formal] yoga.
One who was ignorant of the ritual becomes a knower of the ritual with respect to the sacrifice.
Beginning with Kālāgni and ending with Māyā, which resides within the body of Brahmā;
Śiva, who extends from Viśva to Ananta, is considered the supreme triad of powers (śaktitraya). (ParTri 21)
Whatever exists within that, established on the path of purity,
that subtle and purified [soul] soon attains the knowledge of the Lord.
He who impels that [power] is to be known as Śiva, the omniscient Supreme Lord;
he is all-pervading, stainless, clear, satisfied, self-abiding, and pure. (Paratrimśikā 23)
Just as a great tree exists in the form of a potentiality within the seed of a banyan tree,
so too does this entire world of moving and non-moving beings exist within the seed of the heart.
Thus, for one who knows this according to reality, initiation leading to nirvāṇa occurs without doubt, even though it is devoid of oblations of sesame and clarified butter.
Having performed the ritual placement (nyāsa) on the head, the mouth, the heart, the secret place, and likewise on the body,
one should bind the topknot (śikhā) consecrated twenty-seven times with the mantra.
One should apply the binding of each of the ten directions individually,
having first given three claps with sound for the pacification of obstacles.
Then, one should sprinkle with water consecrated by reciting the Śikhā-mantra the prescribed number of times;
thereafter, all the offerings, beginning with flowers, should be placed in due order upon either the liṅga or the sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila).
The preparation of the seat is performed with a flower consecrated fourteen times;
there the hero should worship the emanation, and thereafter the seat once again.
Having encapsulated the emanation, one should thereafter commence the worship,
[visualizing the deity] fully complete with all principles and adorned with all ornaments.
One should worship the goddess Maheśānī with twenty-seven mantras;
thereafter, one should honor her with fragrant flowers according to one's capacity. (ParTri 31)
One should worship with supreme devotion and offer oneself as well;
thus is sacrifice declared, and this same rule applies to the fire-ritual as well. (Paratriṃśikā 32)

Having properly performed the ritual of worship, one attains success by correctly remembering the seed-syllable (*bīja*). One should meditate upon that seed-syllable— which is devoid of beginning and end, blossoming, situated in the midst of the lunar days, and located within the heart-lotus— and practice it constantly as a portion of the moon.
Thus is the attainment of the fruit of mantra; this is the Rudrayāmala.
Through the practice of this, perfection and omniscience are attained.
